title: Villa Soriano founded
description: Franciscans found a mission that becomes the oldest European settlement in Uruguay.

title: Colonia del Sacramento founded
description: The Portuguese build a fort opposite Buenos Aires, starting a century of rivalry with Spain over the eastern bank of the Río de la Plata.

title: Montevideo founded
description: The governor of Buenos Aires, Bruno Mauricio de Zabala, founds a fortified town to keep the Portuguese out of the bay.

title: First Treaty of San Ildefonso
description: Portugal gives up Colonia del Sacramento to Spain, leaving the whole of the eastern bank in Spanish hands.

title: Cry of Asencio
polity: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
description: Country people rise against the Spanish authorities of Montevideo, beginning the revolution in the Banda Oriental.

title: Battle of Las Piedras
polity: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
description: José Gervasio Artigas defeats the Spanish and goes on to besiege Montevideo.

title: Battle of Tacuarembó
description: The Portuguese destroy the forces of Artigas, who goes into exile in Paraguay as the province is absorbed into Brazil.

title: Landing of the Thirty-Three
description: Juan Antonio Lavalleja crosses from Argentina with a small band to raise the province against Brazilian rule.

title: Declaration of independence
description: An assembly at Florida declares the province independent of Brazil and united with the Argentine provinces.

title: Battle of Ituzaingó
polity: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
description: An Argentine and Oriental army defeats the Brazilians in the largest battle of the Cisplatine War.

title: Preliminary Peace Convention
description: Under British mediation Brazil and Argentina agree that the disputed province will be an independent state.

title: First constitution
description: The constitution of the Oriental State of Uruguay is sworn, a date kept as a national holiday.

title: Massacre of Salsipuedes
description: Troops under President Fructuoso Rivera ambush and kill or capture the Charrúa, nearly ending them as a people.

title: Battle of Carpintería
description: The followers of Oribe and Rivera fight wearing white and red badges, the origin of the Blanco and Colorado parties.

title: Great Siege of Montevideo
description: Blanco forces backed by the Argentine ruler Rosas besiege the Colorado government in Montevideo for more than eight years.

title: Fall of Paysandú
description: Brazilian and Colorado forces take the town after a month's siege, bringing Venancio Flores to power and helping to start the Paraguayan War.

title: School reform
description: A law drafted by José Pedro Varela establishes free and compulsory primary schooling.

title: Batlle y Ordóñez becomes president
description: José Batlle y Ordóñez takes office and over two terms introduces the labour and welfare laws that shape modern Uruguay.

title: Battle of Masoller
description: Government forces defeat the Blanco leader Aparicio Saravia, who dies of his wounds, ending the last of the civil wars.

title: First football World Cup
description: Uruguay hosts the first World Cup and wins it by beating Argentina 4–2 in the final.

title: Terra's coup
description: President Gabriel Terra dissolves parliament and the collegiate council and rules with the support of the police.

title: Graf Spee scuttled
description: The German warship Admiral Graf Spee, which had taken refuge in neutral Montevideo after the Battle of the River Plate, is blown up by her crew.

title: Maracanazo
description: Uruguay beats Brazil 2–1 in Rio de Janeiro to win its second World Cup.

title: Coup of 1973
description: President Juan María Bordaberry closes parliament with the backing of the armed forces, beginning twelve years of dictatorship.

title: Plebiscite of 1980
description: Voters reject a constitution proposed by the military government, starting the return to civilian rule.

title: Democracy restored
description: Julio María Sanguinetti takes office as elected president, ending the military government.

title: Banking crisis
description: A run on the banks after the Argentine collapse forces a bank holiday and brings the deepest recession in the country's modern history.

title: Vázquez elected
description: Tabaré Vázquez of the Broad Front wins the presidency, the first victory of the left over the two traditional parties.

title: Cannabis legalised
description: The Senate passes a law making Uruguay the first country to legalise the production and sale of cannabis.
